findings.F1: The book failed on its falls, not its gain: it earned 20.0 % a year against a deepest fall of 36.3 % (Calmar 0.55 against the 0.75 required), and its daily returns track holding the coins with a correlation of 0.92, because it holds a position on 92 % of bars.
findings.F2: Its three deepest falls (36.3 %, 35.5 % and 33.5 %) are the coins' own declines carried through. Holding the coins lost 59.7 % over the 2021 stretch (w12 to w16) and 59.2 % over the 2022 stretch (w1 to w10), and the book's worst windows are the coins' worst: w7 −0.20 against −0.58, w14 −0.20 against −0.52, w2 −0.18 against −0.46 in summed daily returns.
findings.F3: The grind measure barely grades what follows: the slope t is 0.91 on 4,191 cases, and the unusual move is +0.08 % per 48 hours, 0.011 of the usual 6.56 % move. That is 0.4 times the 0.19 % cost of a round trip, so most of the book's +0.35 % total move per case is the coins' drift.
findings.F4: The forecast's middle carries the effect, not its top. On 48-hour grid cases after a net fall, excess return is −24 bps in the lowest forecast quintile, +37 to +45 bps in quintiles 2 to 4, and only +5 bps in the most even (top) quintile. Flat cases run −14 bps against +21 bps for positive-forecast cases.
findings.F5: The rebound after a 24-hour fall lives in agitated markets, where the coin's 7-day hourly volatility is high against its 30-day volatility. In that upper tercile the 2-day excess return is +98 bps (126 bps total, 1,044 cases), against −11 bps in the calm tercile and −23 bps in the middle one. On all position bars, the top quintile of this ratio earns 1.34 bps per bar and carries 77 % of the book's whole gain; the other quintiles earn −0.00 to 0.23 bps.
findings.F6: Within the agitated tercile the grind grading is still positive (slope t 1.44), while in the calm tercile it turns negative (t −1.28). The grind measure adds something only when volatility has risen.
findings.F7: The rebound also concentrates after a deeper 7-day fall: the lowest 7-day-return tercile gives +56 bps excess over 2 days with slope t 1.45, against −27 bps for the middle tercile.
findings.F8: Exposure held in a mild 30-day decline (30-day return between −17 % and −4.5 %) loses money: −0.23 to −0.27 bps per position bar at a mean allocation of 0.51 to 0.55. Every other 30-day quintile earns +0.20 to +0.71 bps.

ideas.idea: The more a coin has fallen over the last 24 hours in many similar-sized hourly steps rather than in one large hour, the more it rises over the next 2 days, only while its hourly moves over the last 7 days have been larger than over the last 30 days, and the more so the larger that ratio.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a grinding daily decline only once the coin's recent volatility has risen above its monthly norm, and stay out of the same decline in a calm market, where it carries no rebound and only adds the coin's falls to the book.
ideas.name: grind rebound in agitation

ideas.idea: The more a coin's hourly volatility over the last 7 days exceeds its volatility over the last 30 days, the more it rises over the next 2 days after a fall over the last 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: Long exposure after a daily drop is worth taking in proportion to how agitated the coin's recent week has been, which ties the book's risk to the moments that pay rather than to being long almost all the time.
ideas.name: agitated fall rebound

ideas.idea: The deeper a coin's fall over the last 7 days, the more it rises over the next 2 days after a further fall over the last 24 hours, the more so the larger its last 7 days' hourly volatility against its last 30 days'.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy into a daily drop that comes on top of a deep, volatile week, the situation where the 2-day rebound is several times the cost of a round trip.
ideas.name: deep volatile week rebound
